issues.title: Sinestro, Part One
issues.summary: On Oa, the Guardians allow Sinestro to wield a Green Lantern ring again, despite Ganthet’s doubts. Meanwhile, Hal Jordan is stranded on Earth without his ring and struggles to keep his life together. After a misunderstanding involving Carol Ferris, he returns home to find an eviction notice. On Korugar, Sinestro discovers that the Sinestro Corps has enslaved the people he once ruled. He kills a disobedient Corps member and destroys the soldier’s yellow ring. Realizing his former followers have become a threat to his homeworld, Sinestro travels to Earth and finds Hal. He offers to restore Hal’s ring—but only if Hal agrees to follow his orders.

issues.title: With Blood and Rage
issues.summary:
Atrocitus rescues Dex-Starr from a crew of torturers, but the encounter forces him to confront how his rage has begun to lose its purpose. Back on Ysmault, he struggles to command the Red Lanterns, whose limited reasoning makes them difficult to lead. Bleez stands out as unusually intelligent and openly challenges his authority.

Flashbacks recall the massacre of Sector 666 and Atrocitus’ loss of his family, while on Earth an elderly veteran is murdered during a mugging. His grandsons John and Raymond react to the tragedy in very different ways, and their grief deepens the rift between them. Seeking guidance, Atrocitus performs a blood prophecy using Krona’s blood. The visions show suffering and injustice across the universe, giving him a renewed mission: his Corps must become an instrument of vengeance, not merely a pack of raging monsters.

issues.title: Pure Rage
issues.summary:
Atrocitus answers the fury of a child caught in a war on Ghan IX, bringing the Red Lanterns into a conflict where civilians are paying the price. The story emphasizes the pattern that draws the Corps together: people pushed past endurance by cruelty and loss. Atrocitus sees their rage as a call for punishment, though his methods offer little distinction between justice and revenge.

As the Red Lanterns intervene, the conflict turns brutal and the innocent remain in danger despite their arrival. The issue reinforces Atrocitus’ belief that rage can answer oppression, while showing the danger of making an emotion the sole guide to judgment. Back on Ysmault, his doubts about his own Corps and his search for a meaningful purpose continue.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Two
issues.summary: Sinestro offers Hal Jordan a new Green Lantern ring, but Hal attacks him as soon as he puts it on. Sinestro reveals that he can control the ring and shut it down whenever he chooses, making Hal dependent on him. When a bridge collapses in Coast City, Hal tries to save the victims, but Sinestro disables his ring to teach him a lesson. Sinestro then rescues everyone and reconstructs the bridge, demonstrating a more effective use of the ring. Their demonstration is interrupted by Gorgor, a Sinestro Corps member responsible for the disaster. Sinestro kills him and explains that his Corps has become cruel and tyrannical. He needs Hal's help to free Korugar from his own former army.

issues.title: Higher Consciousness
issues.summary:
Atrocitus decides Bleez may be the lieutenant he needs, but first he tries to restore her ability to think clearly. He casts her into Ysmault’s Blood Ocean, where the Red Lantern rage can be tempered into a more focused consciousness. As Bleez sinks beneath the surface, memories return: her family was murdered and she was tortured by the Sinestro Corps. Her rage is not abstract; it comes from a specific history of suffering.

Bleez fights her way back toward the surface with a clearer mind and a stronger sense of purpose. Atrocitus believes he has found a capable second-in-command, but the process has also given Bleez the ability to question him and his leadership. Their relationship shifts from simple obedience to a tense contest over what the Red Lanterns should become.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Three
issues.summary: Hal agrees to accompany Sinestro to Korugar, though he refuses to accept Sinestro's claim of superiority. On Oa, the Guardians strip Ganthet of his emotions and discuss replacing the Green Lantern Corps with a new force. Meanwhile, Hal and Sinestro arrive on Korugar and plan to disable the Sinestro Corps' Central Power Battery. Sinestro draws the Corps members away while Hal enters the battery, but it begins to disintegrate him. As Sinestro watches in horror, the mission appears to have ended in disaster. On Earth, Carol Ferris sees news footage of Hal working alongside Sinestro and cannot believe they have become allies.

issues.title: The Departed
issues.summary:
Suspicious that the Red Lanterns are plotting against him, Atrocitus probes Skallox’s memories by drinking his blood. The fragmented vision suggests that Bleez has been speaking about killing Atrocitus, and he responds by throwing Skallox into the Blood Ocean. He also casts Zilius Zox and Ratchet into it, despite Bleez’s warning that the process could destroy them.

The issue reveals the tragic origins of Ratchet and Skallox: Ratchet was persecuted for seeking physical contact in a society that outlawed it, while Skallox was betrayed and burned alive by the criminal he served. Their suffering explains the rage that brought them to the Corps. Atrocitus continues dispensing violent punishment elsewhere in the universe, but finds no lasting satisfaction. When he returns to Ysmault, he discovers that Krona’s corpse has vanished. The mystery intensifies his paranoia and gives him a new obsession.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Four
issues.summary: Hal is seemingly disintegrated inside the Sinestro Corps' Central Power Battery, while Sinestro struggles to understand what has happened. The battery's reaction to the Green Lantern energy destabilizes it, and Hal eventually emerges alive, though badly shaken. Sinestro's attempt to liberate Korugar grows more complicated as the enslaved Korugarians remain afraid of him because of his own history as their ruler. Arsona and other prisoners resist the Corps, while Sinestro confronts the consequences of the army he created. The pair must find a way to defeat the Corps and its power source before the people of Korugar can truly be free.

issues.title: Kronamania
issues.summary:
Atrocitus blames Bleez for the disappearance of Krona’s corpse and attacks her, but she suggests the impossible: Krona may have returned to life. Atrocitus orders her to retrieve Ratchet, Skallox and Zilius Zox from the Blood Ocean so they can search for the missing Guardian. As the three Red Lanterns recover, their pasts reveal how isolation, betrayal and torture transformed them into beings driven by rage.

On Earth, John Moore watches police violently beat his brother Raymond, who dies from his injuries. John has spent his life suppressing anger and is devastated by his own failure to intervene. His grief and self-loathing finally erupt, and a red ring chooses him. The issue ends with John becoming a Red Lantern, while Atrocitus is still hunting for Krona and does not yet understand who has taken the corpse.

issues.title: Sinestro, Part Five
issues.summary: Hal and Sinestro continue their fight to free Korugar from the Sinestro Corps. The imprisoned Korugarians obtain temporary power rings and try to turn them against Sinestro, but the rings cannot harm their creator. Professor Insidd attempts to find a way to neutralize Sinestro's power battery, only for the battery to respond to Sinestro's commands and kill him. The resistance faces the danger of becoming consumed by revenge, while Sinestro must confront the consequences of the Corps' rule and his own legacy. Hal and Sinestro push toward a final confrontation with the force that has enslaved Korugar.

issues.title: All Too Human
issues.summary:
The red ring transforms Jack Moore into Rankorr, but he has no understanding of the power or the rage consuming him. He returns to his grandfather’s grave and realizes that his family’s deaths have left him with nothing to hold onto. When he tracks down Baxter, the man responsible for his grandfather’s murder, his rage overwhelms him. Rankorr attacks the police van carrying Baxter and kills him with the tombstone he has torn from the grave.

Meanwhile, Atrocitus and Bleez’s rivalry grows more dangerous as each questions the other’s right to lead the Red Lanterns. An old enemy is revealed amid the struggle over Krona’s missing body. Rankorr’s first act of vengeance is complete, but it does not bring peace: he has crossed the line into lethal violence and is now a Red Lantern whose powers and emotions remain dangerously uncontrolled.

issues.title: The Other Hero
issues.summary: With the battle for Korugar over, Sinestro and Hal face the question of what comes next. Sinestro sends Hal back to Earth, where Hal tries to repair his damaged relationship with Carol Ferris and acknowledge the mistakes he has made. Their partnership has shown Hal a different, more ruthless kind of heroism, even as Sinestro remains a deeply troubling ally. On Oa, the Guardians pursue a far more ominous plan: they intend to unleash the First Lantern and build a Third Army to replace the Green Lantern Corps. The victory on Korugar therefore closes one conflict while setting up a much larger threat to the universe.

issues.title: Rebel Yell
issues.summary:
Guy Gardner confronts Rankorr, the first human Red Lantern, as the new ring drives Jack Moore toward uncontrolled violence. Guy tries to reach him by drawing on his own experience with red rage. Rankorr briefly regains enough clarity to ask for help and even saves Guy from being struck by a car, but then rockets away into space, realizing that he may no longer be fully human.

Elsewhere, Bleez attacks a group of surviving Sinestro Corps members and declares a new age for the Red Lanterns. She rejects Atrocitus’ fixation on the past and begins to assert her own command, while the captives warn that Atrocitus remains a formidable threat. The issue closes with Rankorr newly transformed and adrift, Guy unable to follow him, and Bleez openly challenging the existing order—setting up the coming power struggle within the Red Lantern Corps.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part One
issues.summary:
Sinestro explains why he needs Hal Jordan back: the Guardians have returned him to the Green Lantern Corps, but his former Sinestro Corps has taken control of Korugar and he cannot free his homeworld alone. Hal refuses to trust him, yet their argument is interrupted when Indigo-1 and the Indigo Tribe arrive. They seize Sinestro because they believe the Guardians have made a terrible mistake by giving him a green ring. Hal follows them to the Indigo homeworld, determined not to abandon him.

On Oa, the Guardians question Lyssa Drak about the Book of the Black and the First Lantern, showing that they are pursuing a secret plan of their own. On Nok, Hal is captured and finds Black Hand among the prisoners. The issue ends with Hal and Sinestro separated and in the hands of the Tribe: Indigo-1 intends to subject Sinestro to the Indigo light, while Hal has no clear way to rescue him.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Two
issues.summary:
On Nok, Hal and Sinestro are powerless and on the run from the Indigo Tribe. Indigo-1 begins forcing Sinestro through the Tribe’s conversion process. Sinestro violently resists, furious at the idea of being made compassionate, but Indigo-1 overpowers him. In another part of the enormous prison complex, Hal talks with Black Hand, who claims the Indigo light has given him a purpose and the ability to experience emotions beyond death.

Hal tricks Black Hand into cycling his ring through the green light and uses the borrowed energy to recharge his own ring. The charge is only simulated: Hal cannot fly, his protection is unreliable and his constructs may fail. He improvises a construct motorcycle and heads through the vast prison to find Sinestro. The issue ends with Hal still pursuing him, while the Tribe’s secret remains only partly revealed and Sinestro is still under Indigo-1’s control.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Three
issues.summary:
Hal discovers the truth about the Indigo Tribe from Natromo, the last survivor of a people once enslaved on Nok. Natromo explains that he and Abin Sur harnessed the indigo light to make their oppressors feel remorse. Abin later used the same process on Iroque, a murderer who had killed his daughter, and transformed her into Indigo-1. The Tribe is made up of dangerous criminals whose personalities are suppressed by their rings; their apparent compassion is imposed, not freely chosen.

Abin had another reason for creating them: he foresaw a threat from within the Green Lantern Corps and believed the Guardians themselves would become the enemy. Natromo had planned to attack the Guardians with the Tribe, but Hal tells him Abin is dead. Overwhelmed by grief and believing their mission impossible, Natromo destroys the Indigo Central Battery. The rings go dark, freeing Sinestro from the Indigo influence—and releasing the former criminals from the restraints that kept their violence in check. Hal’s attempt to expose the truth has left the Tribe powerless and dangerous.

issues.title: The Secret of the Indigo Tribe, Part Four
issues.summary:
With the Indigo Battery destroyed, Hal and Sinestro must escape from the former Tribe members, who have reverted to their old violent selves. Black Hand abandons the group and throws away his Indigo ring, while Hal finds Natromo and tries to persuade him to rebuild the battery. Natromo says it cannot be restored without a spark of indigo light. Indigo-1 catches up with them and admits she is terrified of returning to the person she was before the ring; when she recalls what compassion made her feel, a tear provides the spark Natromo needs. He restores the battery and the Indigo rings reactivate.

Hal asks Indigo-1 to release Sinestro. She agrees only after asking Hal whether he believes Sinestro can become a hero without being forced to feel compassion. Hal admits that he wants to believe it is possible, and Sinestro is freed from the Tribe’s control. Black Hand, however, refuses to be reclaimed: he jumps from a cliff and dies before his ring can reach him. A black ring emerges and orders him to rise, resurrecting him as a Black Lantern. The arc closes with Sinestro free but still distrusted, while Black Hand’s return launches the next threat.

issues.title: The Revenge of Black Hand, Part One
issues.summary:
Hal and Sinestro leave Nok after the Indigo Tribe releases Sinestro from its influence. Natromo has reversed the bond between their rings: Hal can now shut down Sinestro’s ring, just as Sinestro once controlled Hal’s. When they search for Black Hand, they find only black residue beneath a cliff and assume he killed himself to avoid being forced back into the Tribe. They do not know that the black ring has already resurrected him.

On Earth, Black Hand massacres the customers and staff of a restaurant, then goes to a cemetery and raises the bodies of his own family. He wants to turn the living into the dead so that the world will share his separation from life. Meanwhile, the Guardians track Hal and Sinestro and continue preparing their own campaign against the other Lantern Corps. The issue ends with Black Hand beginning his assault on the living and the Guardians closing in on the two Lanterns.

issues.title: The Revenge of Black Hand, Part Two
issues.summary:
Black Hand uses the Book of the Black to understand his new purpose, but its message unsettles him. The pages insist that Hal Jordan is not his enemy and begin to reveal that Hal will become the greatest Black Lantern. Black Hand attacks Hal and Sinestro, and Hal shoots him in the head to stop him temporarily. The two Lanterns are surrounded by the zombies Black Hand has raised, while their rings are too weak to win a direct fight.

Hal tries to contact Carol Ferris for help, but Black Hand’s power interferes with the signal. Sinestro comes up with a desperate plan: they summon his yellow power battery and use their green rings to destroy it. The resulting explosion severs Black Hand’s control over the undead, but leaves Hal and Sinestro unconscious. Black Hand survives and finds them, reading the Book again as it declares Hal will be the greatest Black Lantern. The immediate zombie attack is halted, but Black Hand remains free—and the Guardians’ plan to eradicate the other Corps is moving forward.

issues.title: The Revenge of Black Hand: Conclusion
issues.summary:
Hal and Sinestro are buried alive after Black Hand defeats them, but Hal digs his way out and refuses Black Hand’s offer to resurrect his father. Black Hand tries to exploit Hal’s grief, promising to bring back the dead as real people rather than mindless zombies. Hal rejects the temptation and fights him; Sinestro joins the battle, and together they summon Hal’s power battery to recharge their rings and attack Black Hand and his undead army.

Elsewhere, the Guardians break into the Chamber of Shadows, where a hidden group of Oans has kept the First Lantern imprisoned. They kill one of the guardians of the prison, seize the First Lantern and take him away. Returning to Earth, they empower Black Hand, who creates a vast black vortex that pulls Hal and Sinestro into the Dead Zone; their rings interpret the event as their deaths. The Guardians then imprison Black Hand for later use and begin creating the Third Army, believing they can eliminate free will by replacing the Lantern Corps. The annual ends with Hal and Sinestro missing, the First Lantern in the Guardians’ hands and the Third Army about to be unleashed.

issues.title: The New Normal
issues.summary:
Simon Baz’s origin begins in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks, which have shaped how strangers treat his Arab-American family. Years later, Simon steals a van to earn money after losing his job at a car factory, only to discover that it contains a bomb. He abandons the vehicle before it crashes into an empty building and is arrested as a suspected terrorist. During a brutal interrogation, Simon insists that he knew nothing about the bomb and explains that he had been trying to support his sister Sira and her son.

As the agents prepare to torture him, a Green Lantern ring breaks into the facility and chooses Simon. He uses it to escape, but crashes in a field and loses consciousness. The ring remains beside him with a message, while Amanda Waller learns what happened and Batman and Cyborg begin investigating the new Lantern. In the closing scene, Hal Jordan and Sinestro are shown alive in the dark realm they were pulled into after Black Hand’s attack. Simon has received the ring, but neither he nor the world yet knows why it chose him.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Actions and Reactions
issues.summary:
The Guardians unleash the first soldiers of the Third Army, a force created from the power of the First Lantern. These pale creatures assimilate living beings and turn them into more soldiers, spreading the Guardians’ attempt to impose order by erasing individuality. On Earth, Simon Baz is still regarded as a criminal and struggles to make peace with his sister Sira, whose husband Nazir remains in a coma after an accident Simon blames himself for.

Simon goes to meet Sira at their old school, but the Justice League arrives and demands answers about Hal Jordan’s disappearance and Simon’s new ring. Batman and the others do not trust him, and the encounter becomes a fight rather than a welcome. The issue closes with Simon facing the League while the Third Army begins its expansion elsewhere. His first major test is not a clean victory over a villain: he has to survive the suspicion of the very heroes who should be helping him.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
The Third Army begins assimilating people on distant worlds while the Guardians manipulate Guy Gardner’s position inside the Corps. On Oa, Guy is publicly named Lantern Sentinel. He chooses John Stewart for an escort mission involving ambassadors from two warring cultures, but the Guardians summon John away to investigate strange activity among the remains of Mogo. They then exploit Guy’s concern for his family: Xar, the alien who killed Green Lantern trainees, is sent toward Earth, and Guy abandons part of his escort mission to stop him.

The Guardians have anticipated Guy’s choice. They order Xar to attack the delegation and leave no survivors, setting Guy up to take the blame. As Guy’s team approaches Saturn, the Third Army attacks and assimilates Vandor. The issue ends with the Corps suffering its first visible losses to the new enemy and Guy being maneuvered into a situation where his instinct to protect his family can be used against him.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Kyle Rayner returns to Earth and discovers that Carol Ferris has become a Star Sapphire. Carol helps Kyle understand that to master the emotional spectrum he must experience each emotion rather than simply collect rings. She brings him to Atrocitus, who agrees to train him in rage. Atrocitus takes Kyle to a war-torn place and forces him to witness a father being murdered in front of his child. Kyle is horrified, but the experience triggers the red light within him.

Kyle unleashes rage against the killers and proves he can wield a Red Lantern’s power, though the lesson is brutal and morally unsettling. Atrocitus leaves him to continue his journey, while Carol and Kyle prepare to seek out the next Lantern who can teach him another part of the spectrum. The issue ends with Kyle having gained access to red energy, but at the cost of being forced to confront how easily righteous anger can become destructive.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
On Arhtky, Taya and her sister try to escape the warlord Cord, whose men have enslaved them. After Taya’s sister is killed, Taya briefly finds shelter with a couple in the woods, but the man betrays them to Cord. The Red Lanterns arrive and punish Cord’s people, only to discover that the Third Army has invaded the area. Its creatures are resistant to the Red Lanterns’ usual attacks and assimilate their victims instead of simply killing them.

One Red Lantern is consumed, and Taya herself is transformed into one of the creatures. Atrocitus notices that their eyes may be vulnerable and that the enemy seems to share sensations through a collective mind. The battle ends with the Red Lanterns forced to retreat with more questions than answers: their violence cannot stop the Third Army, and a person they tried to save has become part of it.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Courage
issues.summary:
The Justice League continues to question Simon Baz, whose criminal record makes it difficult for him to earn their trust. Simon insists that he did not know the stolen van contained a bomb, but his anger and refusal to submit quietly make the League wary. At the same time, the Guardians’ plan becomes harder to hide: the Third Army is spreading, and the Corps is being ordered to respond without being told that the Guardians themselves created the creatures.

The issue’s two conflicts sharpen without being resolved. Simon remains under suspicion rather than being accepted as a hero, and the Green Lanterns are still following orders from leaders who are concealing the true nature of the threat. The ending leaves Simon isolated on Earth while the Guardians continue the next stage of their campaign.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Guy Gardner’s squad is overwhelmed by the Third Army near Saturn. The creatures assimilate the Lanterns one by one, and Vandor is among those lost. Guy survives the attack, but the Guardians use the disaster to blame him for abandoning his assignment. Meanwhile, Kilowog and Salaak investigate why new power rings have stopped reaching recruits and discover that the Guardians have blocked the rings from leaving Oa.

Guy returns to Oa expecting to explain his actions, only to be publicly accused of disobedience and responsibility for the deaths of his squad and the peace delegation. The Guardians demand that he resign, and Guy does. He leaves Oa stripped of his ring and rank, while John is kept away from the central conflict by the assignment to investigate Mogo. The issue ends with Guy disgraced and the Guardians having removed one of the Corps’ most outspoken Lanterns from their command.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Kyle continues his training with Indigo-1 and is forced to confront fear when Arkillo challenges him. The lesson is not simply to overpower his opponent: Kyle has to recognize the emotion and learn how to direct it. He manages to turn the encounter around and survive, showing that he can channel another colour of the spectrum without losing himself completely.

Carol joins Kyle, and they decide to seek Larfleeze, whose orange light represents avarice. Arkillo follows, partly because he wants to find Sinestro. The issue ends with Kyle, Carol and Arkillo travelling toward Larfleeze’s world in an uneasy alliance. The Third Army remains a looming threat, but this chapter’s immediate resolution is Kyle’s survival of Arkillo’s test and the team’s next destination.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
The Red Lanterns return to Arhtky and exploit a weakness in the Third Army: its eyes. By targeting them, Atrocitus and his team begin to win the fight. Rankorr hesitates because he senses traces of Taya within the creature she became, but he finally uses the tactic and helps defeat the attackers in the immediate battle.

Atrocitus takes samples of the creatures back to Ysmault and uses blood magic to learn that they are connected to the Guardians and are vulnerable to non-organic matter. The encounter also reveals that the Red Lanterns need a synthetic means of defence. Atrocitus sends Rankorr to Earth to confront the source of his rage and become a fully realized Red Lantern; Bleez accompanies him, while Dex-Starr follows for his own reasons. The issue ends with the Red Lanterns splitting up on new missions and Atrocitus turning from direct combat toward building a countermeasure.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Guy Gardner struggles to live without his ring after the Guardians force him out of the Corps. His attempt to intervene in a police operation involving his family goes badly, reinforcing the impression that he is reckless and unstable. Meanwhile, John Stewart and Fatality investigate what is happening to Mogo’s remains and discover that the Guardians have sent John away from Oa for a reason: the fragments are being used in a destructive scheme, not simply reassembling naturally.

John realizes that the Guardians are manipulating events to remove the Lanterns who might oppose them. Guy’s personal crisis and John’s investigation converge on the same truth: the Guardians are deliberately weakening the Corps. The issue ends with Guy’s life in turmoil and John increasingly suspicious of his leaders, while neither yet has enough power or evidence to stop the plan.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Kyle reaches Larfleeze’s world to learn how to wield the orange light of avarice. Larfleeze refuses to share his power freely, but Carol persuades him to train Kyle by offering to help him find what he most wants: the truth about his family and his own name. Kyle must charge his ring in the orange power battery while fighting Larfleeze, an arrangement that makes the lesson as dangerous as it is necessary.

When the Third Army attacks, Larfleeze does the unthinkable and helps Kyle access the orange light. Sayd holds the creatures back long enough for Kyle and the others to escape, but she is killed in the attack. Kyle succeeds in gaining the orange power, yet the victory costs him an ally and leaves him indebted to Larfleeze. The issue ends with Ganthet, under the Guardians’ influence, recognizing Kyle as a threat and preparing to confront him.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Innocent Lives
issues.summary:
Simon Baz and Guy Gardner meet for the first time as the Third Army continues to spread. Guy has been expelled from the Corps and is being held by the authorities; Simon, still considered a criminal, arrives in the middle of the crisis. Their encounter is tense, but it becomes clear that both men are being targeted by the Guardians’ plan. When the Third Army attacks, Simon and Guy have to fight together rather than argue about their pasts.

The issue also returns to Hal Jordan and Sinestro, who remain trapped in the Dead Zone after their apparent deaths. On Earth, Simon and Guy survive the immediate attack, but their alliance is only beginning and neither has the support of the Guardians. The ending brings the new Lantern and the disgraced veteran together against a common enemy, while leaving Hal and Sinestro’s fate unresolved.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Atrocitus returns to the dead world of Ryut and awakens a squadron of Manhunters he once defeated. Believing the mechanical soldiers can serve as a weapon against the Third Army, he uses blood magic to reactivate them outside the Guardians’ control. The plan is dangerous: the Manhunters were created by the Guardians and were responsible for the massacre that shaped Atrocitus’ life.

On Earth, Rankorr and Bleez pursue the man responsible for the murder of Rankorr’s grandfather. When Rankorr finally confronts the source of his hatred, he struggles to decide whether becoming a Red Lantern means giving himself entirely to vengeance. Meanwhile, the reactivated Manhunters turn on Atrocitus instead of obeying him and open fire. The issue ends with Atrocitus under attack by the very army he hoped to command, while Rankorr’s personal mission forces him to question what his rage is for.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
John Stewart and Fatality investigate the remains of Mogo and discover that the Guardians have turned them into a weapon. A vessel is using Mogo’s fragments to fire a destructive green beam at a planet. John and Fatality stop the attack, but John realizes that the Guardians deliberately sent him away from Oa to keep him from interfering with their real plan.

On Earth, Guy Gardner is in custody after losing his ring and rank. Simon Baz and the small Lantern B’dg help him escape when the Third Army attacks. Guy immediately focuses on getting his family and civilians to safety, while Simon fights beside him despite still being treated as a suspect. The issue ends with Guy and Simon working together against the Guardians’ soldiers, and John understanding that the Guardians have deliberately isolated the Lanterns so they can destroy the Corps from within.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Trial by Fire
issues.summary:
Simon Baz finally meets Guy Gardner as the Third Army’s assault threatens to overwhelm the Corps. Simon has been trying to prove himself while the Justice League and the authorities continue to regard him with suspicion; Guy has been expelled and publicly blamed for the Guardians’ engineered disaster. Their meeting is tense, but the Guardians’ soldiers attack before they can settle their differences, forcing them to fight side by side.

Elsewhere, the Guardians draw more power from the imprisoned First Lantern, accelerating their plan to replace the Corps. The story also returns to Hal Jordan and Sinestro in the Dead Zone: they are alive, but still trapped and unable to return to the fight. The issue closes with Simon and Guy surviving the Third Army attack and recognizing that they may have to rely on each other, while the Guardians’ plan moves toward its next stage, Wrath of the First Lantern.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Kyle Rayner’s attempt to master the full emotional spectrum is interrupted by a Third Army attack. After learning to channel the red, indigo, violet and orange lights, he is closer to combining the colours, but the process remains unstable. Ganthet, now under the Guardians’ control, confronts Kyle and tries to stop him from completing the task.

Kyle manages to overcome Ganthet and forces the Guardian to retreat, demonstrating that he can use the combined spectrum against one of the Guardians’ own. The issue ends with Kyle deciding to join the fight against the Third Army rather than continue training in isolation. He has not yet mastered the White Lantern power, but his ability to unite the colours has made him a key part of the resistance.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army: Finale
issues.summary:
The Third Army’s assault reaches Oa, and the Guardians shut down the Green Lantern Corps they once created. Guy Gardner, Simon Baz and B’dg try to stop the attack while the Guardians exploit the chaos to carry out their plan. Guy’s ring has been taken from him, but he still throws himself into the fight; Simon uses his new powers to help defend the others and tries to reach Hal Jordan and Sinestro, who are trapped in the Dead Zone.

The battle becomes a desperate attempt to keep the Corps from being erased. The Guardians’ Third Army overwhelms the Lanterns, and the Guardians move to eliminate their own organization rather than allow it to resist. The ending does not restore the Corps or defeat the Guardians: the Third Army has done its intended damage, the Guardians remain in control, and the surviving Lanterns are left facing the consequences. The final pages point directly to the next event, Wrath of the First Lantern, as the First Lantern’s role becomes the next central mystery.

issues.title: Rise of the Third Army
issues.summary:
Atrocitus’ attempt to command the Manhunters collapses when the machines turn against him. The androids attack their supposed master, forcing Atrocitus to fight the same kind of weapon that once destroyed his people. He survives the initial assault and begins to understand that the Manhunters cannot simply be controlled by blood magic; their programming and history make them dangerous allies at best.

Atrocitus fights his way back into the confrontation and destroys the Manhunters’ Alpha, breaking their attack and reclaiming control of the situation. The victory is costly and does not erase the old hatred between him and the machines. The issue ends with Atrocitus having defeated the immediate rebellion, but the Third Army remains a threat and his plan to use a synthetic army is far from secure.
